name: KoboWave Technologies
tagline: From one cracked screen to code that carries Africa's money.

ownerCharacter.name: Engr. Kelechi Adebayo
ownerCharacter.look: Late 20s, slim, round glasses, teal hoodie over white tee, grey joggers, orange sneakers, always carrying a sticker-covered laptop with a tiny screwdriver behind one ear.
ownerCharacter.backstory: Kelechi fixed cracked phone screens under an umbrella in Ikeja and spent the profit on night browsing at a cyber cafe, learning to code from free videos. One customer asked, "You fit build app?" Kelechi said yes first, then learned how.

storyline.title: Umbrella Repair Stand
storyline.stage: A wooden table and umbrella at Computer Village, fixing phones and flashing software.
storyline.story: Kelechi swaps screens by day. Traders keep asking for a simple page to show their goods online. Each small job pays for one more hour of learning. If the stand fails, the dream stops at the umbrella.
storyline.unlock: Product board, first dev desk and the Shop Page line.

storyline.title: Night Class at the Cafe
storyline.stage: A rented corner seat in Bright Byte Cyber Cafe with one borrowed desktop.
storyline.story: NEPA takes light mid-code and unsaved work vanishes. Kelechi learns to save every five minutes and ships a first invoice app for a provisions seller. One happy customer tells ten others.
storyline.unlock: Invoice and Stock App line, plus a small UPS battery.

storyline.title: Two Laptops, One Room
storyline.stage: A one-room app studio in a Yaba face-me-I-face-you flat, with a friend as co-founder.
storyline.story: Old classmate Ngozi joins as designer. Clients want everything by Friday and pay by next month. The studio must choose: keep doing one-off jobs, or build one product that many businesses subscribe to.
storyline.unlock: Sales desk queue, first junior developer and monthly subscriptions.

storyline.title: The Pay Link Idea
storyline.stage: A shared co-working floor in Yaba with six desks and a noisy generator downstairs.
storyline.story: A tailor loses a big order because the buyer cannot pay by transfer on time. Kelechi builds a pay link over one weekend. It works, but moving people's money needs a licence, a partner bank and real care.
storyline.unlock: Pay Link Checkout line and the trip to Abuja for approval.

storyline.title: Seed Money, Real Pressure
storyline.stage: A full Yaba office floor with a glass meeting room, product wall and server closet.
storyline.story: Investor Aunty Folake offers seed money for a slice of the company. Now there is a board, a salary bill and a runway clock. Spend wisely and grow, or burn the cash and start begging for a bridge.
storyline.unlock: Funding rounds, runway meter, senior developers and a manager.

storyline.title: Series A and the Rack Room
storyline.stage: A three-floor KoboWave building in Lagos with its own server room and delivery bay.
storyline.story: One Friday the cloud goes down and every shop on KoboWave cannot collect money. Never again. Kelechi raises a bigger round, buys real servers and opens Nairobi so the service has a second home.
storyline.unlock: Server racks, Cloud Rack Plan line, Nairobi office and machines.

storyline.title: Five Cities, One Codebase
storyline.stage: A campus in Lagos with offices in Nairobi, Cairo and London and a team of hundreds.
storyline.story: Every country has its own rules, currency and holidays. A rival copies the product and poaches staff with big offers. Kelechi must keep people happy, keep data safe and keep the service up everywhere.
storyline.unlock: Country offices as branches, payroll suite and data protection audits.

storyline.title: The Unicorn Bell
storyline.stage: KoboWave Tower in Lagos, two data centres and a San Francisco office with a rooftop garden.
storyline.story: A new round values KoboWave at over one billion dollars. Kelechi rings a bell at the old repair stand, now a free coding school. The job now is to stay honest, stay up and train the next builders.
storyline.unlock: Unicorn status, free coding school and the pan-African expansion map.

howItFitsTheEngine: The player picks feature tickets off the product board and server parts off the delivery bay truck, then carries tickets to developer desks and parts to server racks. Developers and racks turn them into shipped app features. The player carries those to the sales desk, where shop owners, school bursars and bank managers queue to subscribe and pay.

moneyMechanics.rule: Fee per payment, with a cap
moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Each Pay Link payment earns 1.5% plus N100, never more than N2,000. The N100 is waived on payments under N2,500. Payments from abroad earn 3.9%. Many small payments beat one giant one.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Nigerian payment processors publish local card fees of 1.5% + N100 capped at N2,000, and 3.9% on international cards.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Seed gives about $2m for 20% of the company. Series A gives about $15m for another 20%. Cash arrives at once, but your share of daily profit drops to 80%, then 64%.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Lagos seed rounds run about $1m to $3m. Nigerian Series A rounds in 2025 ranged from $11m to $22m.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Salaries leave on the 28th. A junior dev costs N300,000 and a senior N2,000,000 a month. If cash covers under 3 months of pay, staff slow by 25% until you sell more or raise.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Startups track burn and months of runway. Developer pay is the biggest cost for most Nigerian tech firms.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: The office generator drinks 6 litres an hour at about N1,650 a litre, near N80,000 for an 8-hour day. If fuel runs out, racks stop and subscribers leave. Solar cuts the bill by 70%.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Lagos offices and server rooms run on diesel when grid power fails. Average diesel was about N1,648 a litre in March 2026.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Past 200 customers you must register, hire a Data Protection Officer and file an audit by 31 March. Late filing adds 50% to the fee. Ignore it and pay N10m or 2% of yearly income.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Nigerian firms of major importance register with the data regulator and file yearly audit returns by 31 March.

moneyMechanics.howItWorks: Pay Link money sits in a locked settlement vault and goes to sellers next day. You only keep the fee. Settle on time for 30 days to earn a trust star and 10% more customers.
moneyMechanics.realBasis: Licensed payment firms must keep customer funds separate and settle merchants on a fixed schedule.

travel.why: Meet the central bank and data regulator teams for your payments licence and yearly audit.
Open the East Africa office, hire engineers and inspect the second data centre.
Launch the North Africa office and sign a partner bank for Arabic-language checkout.
Serve diaspora customers sending money home and meet investors for the next round.
Pitch global investors, visit the cloud partner and speak at a big tech conference.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Aunty Folake Bankole
rivalsAndAllies.line: I no dey invest in slides, my dear. Show me customers wey pay you twice.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Dayo Zest of ZapPadi
rivalsAndAllies.line: Nice feature, Kelechi. We go launch our own version by Monday.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Mrs. Hadiza Umar
rivalsAndAllies.line: Your app is fine. Now show me where you keep people's data.

rivalsAndAllies.name: Mama Kelechi
rivalsAndAllies.line: This your computer work, e dey pay? Ehen, then chop before you code.

events.name: Light Don Go
events.text: Grid power is out. Generator kicks in and diesel burns twice as fast today.

events.name: Trader Went Viral
events.text: A shoe seller's Shop Page trends online. Double queue at the sales desk today.

events.name: Bug in Production
events.text: A release broke checkout. Carry 3 fix tickets to a senior dev before customers leave.

events.name: Hackathon Win
events.text: Your juniors won a weekend hackathon. All developer desks work 20% faster today.

events.name: Rival Poaching
events.text: ZapPadi offers your senior dev more pay. Give a raise or lose that desk for a day.

events.name: Server Parts Stuck
events.text: The delivery truck is held at the port. No server parts until this evening.

events.name: Clean Audit
events.text: The data audit passed with no issues. Trust rises and big companies join the queue.

events.name: School Fees Season
events.text: Schools are collecting fees with Pay Link. Payment income is up 50% today.

endgame: KoboWave is a billion-dollar company with a Lagos tower, two data centres and offices in Nairobi, Cairo, London and San Francisco, carrying payments for millions of African businesses while its free school trains the next coders.
risksToHandleCarefully: Show the cyber cafe only as a place to learn, never for scams. Customer money and data stay protected. Funding is not a gamble or loot box. No promise of real income. Hacking appears only as attacks to defend against. Staff are adults.

research.claim: Nigerian developers earn a median of about N300,000 a month as juniors and N2,000,000 as seniors, with seniors ranging from N1m to N4m.
Lagos seed rounds in 2026 typically run about $1m to $3m, usually as a post-money SAFE or a priced round.
Nigerian startups raised $442.8m in 2025, with Series A rounds of $11m, $11m, $20m and $22m among the named deals.
A leading Nigerian payment processor charges 1.5% + N100 on local payments, waives the N100 under N2,500, caps fees at N2,000 and charges 3.9% on international cards.
Nigeria's average diesel price was N1,648.08 a litre in March 2026, up from N1,420.17 in February.
Major data controllers in Nigeria must file audit returns by 31 March each year, with a 50% late penalty and sanctions up to N10m or 2% of annual gross revenue.
